description: We are NOVA CODE, a team of Mechatronics Engineering students interested in research, space exploration, and NASA missions. We enjoy learning about aerospace technology and developing websites and interactive experiences that make science more accessible. We welcome teammates with an interest or experience in design, web development, research, or science communication.
summary: Space Relics is an interactive educational web experience developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It brings attention to equipment and artifacts left behind by space missions on the Moon and Mars. Participants join a mission, explore a navigation map, investigate historical objects through photographs and cited sources, and complete quizzes and mini-games. The experience also tracks mission progress and generates a final report. Space Relics addresses the “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge by turning overlooked hardware into stories about exploration, engineering, and scientific discovery. The project is important because it helps preserve the legacy of these missions and makes space science more engaging and accessible to a wider audience.
details:
Space Relics is an interactive educational web application about space exploration. Users take on the role of mission commanders, navigate a mission, and explore artifacts and equipment left on the Moon and Mars. Each discovery includes information, photographs from credited NASA sources, mini-games, and questions. Progress tracking, points, and badges connect the activities into a mission that concludes with a final report. The application also offers content in Spanish and English, ambient music, and text-to-speech.

The project turns lesser-known space artifacts into stories people can explore, helping make science and engineering more accessible. Its format combines research with game elements to encourage curiosity and interest in space missions.

We developed the project with the help of Lovable and AI, using web technologies such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. We used publicly available NASA photographs and sources, credited in the submission. The application runs in a web browser on a computer or phone and requires no specialized hardware. We considered clear communication, accessibility, reliable sources, and compatibility across devices.
